title: Chapter 70: Peony for the Soon Departed 2
content:
Chapter 70

Peony for the Soon Departed 2

Madam Jin’s brow snapped down. "Zixun!" she barked.

At that, the smirk on Wei Wuxian’s face vanished completely.

"Upbringing?" he murmured.

He turned his head slowly, his voice dropping an octave. "Crooked path?"

Lan Wangji’s tone went deep, laced with warning. "Wei Ying."

Jin Zixun and his lackeys caught the sudden shift in the air, going rigid under his gaze. A razor-thin smile pulled at the corner of Wei Wuxian’s mouth. "You really want to know why I don't carry a sword? Fine. I don't mind telling you."

He pivoted to face the crowd, every syllable dripping with cold, measured deliberate weight. "I don't carry one because I want every single one of you to know this: even without a blade, relying purely on what you spit on as a 'crooked path,' I can leave the lot of you eating my dust. You couldn't catch up to me if you tried."

A stunned, ringing silence fell across the glade.

No disciple from any noble clan had ever dared utter something so unhinged, so wildly arrogant in broad daylight, right to the faces of the sect leaders. After a beat of absolute paralysis, Jin Zixun exploded. "Wei Wuxian! You're nothing more than the son of a common servant—how dare you act so high and mighty?!"

Lan Wangji’s eyes narrowed into blades. Wei Wuxian’s pupils shrank to needlepoints, his right hand twitching toward the dark wood of Chenqing tucked into his sash. The clearing smelled like dry kindling waiting for a match.

"A-Xian!"

A soft voice broke through the tension.

The coiled fury in Wei Wuxian’s chest snapped loose. He turned, blinking. "Shijie?"

Jiang Yanli waved him over gently. "A-Xian, come stand behind me."

Wei Wuxian hesitated, freezing mid-step. Madame Jin tightened her grip on Jiang Yanli's arm, warning, "A-Li, stay out of their mess. Don't get involved."

Offering Madame Jin a small, apologetic smile, Jiang Yanli pulled her hands free and stepped forward, planting herself firmly in front of Wei Wuxian. She dipped into a polite, formal curtsy before Jin Zixun and his retinue.

The sudden shift caught Jin Zixun off guard; a few disciples awkwardly returned the gesture, while others just stood there blinking. In a soft, delicate cadence, Jiang Yanli looked up at Jin Zixun. "Young Master Jin, if I understood you correctly, you believe A-Xian broke the rules and acted far too arrogantly by taking a third of the prey on Mount Baifeng for himself. I... have never heard of such a thing happening before. It seems he truly caused everyone quite a bit of trouble, so I would like to apologize to you all on his behalf."

With that, she bowed deeply, offering a grave and earnest apology.

"Shijie!" Wei Wuxian protested, stepping forward.

She remained bowed, angling her face just enough to give him an almost imperceptible shake of her head. He had no choice but to bite his tongue, his knuckles turning white as his fists clenched at his sides.

Across the clearing, Jin Zixuan stood watching with an unreadable, conflicted expression. Jin Zixun, on the other hand, made zero effort to hide the smug triumph written all over his face.

He let out a booming laugh. "Lady Jiang is truly sensible and dignified! What your shidi did was completely out of line, and he certainly made a mess of things for everyone. But since you understand the error, for your sake and Sect Leader Jiang’s, there’s no need for an apology. After all, the Yunmeng Jiang and Lanling Jin clans are practically brothers!"

He puffed out his chest, practically glowing with smug superiority. The blood burned hot in Wei Wuxian’s veins, the bones in his hands cracking under the pressure of his grip. He was just about to snap when Jiang Yanli finished her bow and straightened up.

Her expression was calm, perfectly serious. "However... although I have never taken part in a grand hunt myself, there is one thing I do know. Throughout history, in every single grand hunt ever held, I have never once heard of a rule stating that one person is forbidden from hunting too much."

The triumphant smirks across the clearing froze dead in their tracks.

Jiang Yanli tilted her head slightly. "So, when you say A-Xian broke the rules... exactly which rule did he break?"

This time, it was Wei Wuxian who let out a loud, unapologetic bark of laughter.

Jin Zixun’s face turned an ugly, sickly green, but not a single rebuttal left his mouth. For one, he’d never seen Jiang Yanli take a stand like this and had no idea how to push back without crossing a line—both Madame Jin and Jiang Cheng doted on her fiercely, and he didn't dare pick that fight. But more importantly... if you actually checked the books, there really wasn't a damn rule about it.

Before the silence stretched too thin, someone in the crowd couldn't hold back. In moments like these, Sect Leader Yao was always the first to jump in. "Lady Jiang, you can't look at it like that. Sure, some rules aren't written down in black and white, but everyone knows them in their hearts, and everyone plays along."

Another cultivator shouted from the ranks, "How much prey is on Mount Baifeng to begin with? Five hundred at most? And how many cultivators are out here today? Over five thousand! Everyone is fighting tooth and nail for scraps as it is, and he goes and sweeps up that much game using malicious underhanded tricks! What are the rest of us supposed to do?!"

Wei Wuxian scoffed, opening his mouth to fire back, but Jiang Yanli caught his wrist, murmuring, "Hush now."

A disgruntled voice chimed in from the back, "Exactly! If he hadn't pulled that stunt, I wouldn't be sitting here empty-handed without a single catch!"

Jiang Yanli looked toward the speaker, her voice gentle but firm. "Yet... is it his fault that others couldn't catch anything?"

The man choked on his breath.

She continued smoothly, "Isn't a hunt meant to be a test of pure skill? Even if the fierce corpses and ghosts are gone, aren't the monsters and beasts still roaming the woods? Even if he hadn't taken that third of the quarry—even if he hadn't entered the hunt at all—those who couldn't catch anything still wouldn't have caught anything. The methods A-Xian uses may differ from the rest of you, but they are techniques he cultivated through his own ability. You cannot brand him as a practitioner of evil simply because the rest of the field was denied a share of the spoils."

The crowd that had egged Jin Zixun on went completely silent, their faces turning as sour as their ringleader's. Yet hemmed in by her status, nobody dared yell at her directly.

Jiang Yanli held her ground, her back straight as an arrow. "Furthermore, a hunt is a hunt. Why bring his family's upbringing into this? A-Xian is a disciple of our Yunmeng Jiang Clan. He grew up alongside my brother and me, and our bond is deeper than blood. To hear you casually spit out 'the son of a common servant' to his face... forgive me, but I cannot accept that. Therefore..."

She lifted her chin, her voice ringing clear across the glade. "I expect Young Master Jin Zixun to apologize to Wei Wuxian of the Yunmeng Jiang Clan!"

If anyone else had dared demand an apology from him, Jin Zixun would have slapped them across the jaw on the spot. His face darkened to an ashen purple, his jaw clamped shut. Jiang Yanli didn't blink, keeping her gaze locked on him with quiet, unyielding poise.

Madame Jin stepped in to smooth things over. "A-Li, why take it so seriously? It's just squabbling between boys, don't let it upset you."

"Madam," Jiang Yanli murmured softly, "A-Xian is my little brother. When someone insults him, to me, it is no small matter."

Madame Jin shot a sharp glare at her nephew, letting out a frosty tsk. "Zixun. Did you hear that?"

"Aunt!" Jin Zixun sputtered.

Demanding he apologize to Wei Wuxian was asking him to swallow hot coals. Madame Jin knew his pig-headed pride all too well, and the whole affair was giving her a headache. If Jin Zixun apologized now, he'd throw an unholy tantrum the second they returned to Carp Tower—she was half-tempted to grab him by the scruff and force his head down just to get it over with.

Right on cue, two streaks of spiritual light cut through the canopy as Jin Guangyao and Lan Xichen descended into the clearing.

Lan Wangji dipped his head. "Brother."

Lan Xichen looked around, surprised. "Wangji? What are you doing here?"

Jin Guangyao chimed in with an easy smile, "Everyone, did something happen over here?"

The second he landed, both Jin Zixun and Madame Jin found the perfect lightning rod to vent their boiling frustration. Before Jin Guangyao could even straighten his robes, Madame Jin rounded on him. "Still smiling! A mess of this scale blows up and you actually have the nerve to beam at me?! This is the grand hunt you organized? Useless!"

Jin Guangyao’s signature, effortless smile dropped in an instant under the verbal lashing. He lowered his head obediently. "Mother, what happened?"

Madame Jin sneered, "What happened? Don't you have eyes? Aren't you supposed to be so brilliant at reading the room?"

While Jin Guangyao swallowed the scolding, Jin Zixun cut in, desperate to derail the topic of an apology: "A third of the game across the entire mountain is gone! How are over five thousand cultivators supposed to hunt now?!"

Lan Xichen intervened smoothly, "Lianfang-zun is already making arrangements to expand the perimeter of the hunting grounds. Please, everyone, calm yourselves."

With Ze-wu-jun stepping in, Jin Zixun knew he couldn't keep barking at Jin Guangyao without looking uncouth. Gritting his teeth, he threw his bow to the dirt with a sneer. "This hunt is an absolute farce! Forget it, I'm not wasting my time. I withdraw."

Jin Guangyao started, stepping forward. "Zixun, the arrangements are almost finished. Give us half an incense stick at most—"

Sect Leader Yao joined in, "Young Master Jin, there's really no need for that!"

"The hunt has lost all semblance of fairness, so what the hell am I waiting for? Deal with it yourselves!" Jin Zixun snapped, turning to rally his retinue to fly off.

Jin Guangyao rushed over to coax him down, but the crowd fractured instantly—some shouted that they were leaving with Jin Zixun, while others lingered, reluctant to forfeit their shot at glory. The clearing descended into absolute chaos.

Jiang Yanli gave a quiet sigh and turned to Madame Jin. "Madame, forgive me for causing you trouble."

Madame Jin brushed it off with a wave of her hand. "What nonsense are you talking about? If you want to yell at that thick-headed boy, go right ahead, I won't stop you! If you're still mad, I'll beat him for you."

"No, really, it's fine..." Jiang Yanli said softly. "I think... I'll take my leave now."

Madame Jin quickly caught her arm. "Back to the pavilion, right? Let me have Zixuan walk us back."

As she spoke, she threw aggressive, unsubtle eye signals at Jin Zixuan, who had been lingering awkwardly on the sidelines the entire time.

Jiang Yanli kept her eyes down. "There's no need. I have a few things to say to A-Xian; he can escort me back."

Madame Jin’s brows pinched, casting a wary, displeased sweep over Wei Wuxian. "Two young, unmarried people... wandering off without supervision, isn't that improper?"

"A-Xian is my brother," Jiang Yanli replied simply.

"A-Li, please don't be mad at me," Madame Jin coaxed, her voice softening. "Tell me what that stubborn, brainless brat did this time, and I'll make sure he gets on his knees and begs for your forgiveness."

Jiang Yanli gave a gentle shake of her head. "Truly, Madam. Please, don't force him."

"Who's forcing him?!" Madame Jin insisted. "No one is forcing anyone!"

Wei Wuxian bowed his chin slightly. "Pardon us, Madame Jin."

He and Jiang Yanli dipped into a shared curtsy and turned on their heels. Madame Jin was still gripping Jiang Yanli’s sleeve, reluctant to let go, when Jin Zixuan suddenly broke into a dead sprint toward them, hollering at the top of his lungs:

"Lady Jiang!"

Wei Wuxian pretended his ears had stopped working, tugging Jiang Yanli along. "Shijie, walk faster."

Jin Zixuan bellowed again, his voice cracking: "You've got it all wrong, Lady Jiang"

At that volume, playing deaf was out of the question. Wei Wuxian and Jiang Yanli turned around in unison. The commotion drew the eyes of Jin Zixun’s lingering mob as well, everyone blinking in utter bewilderment, wondering what on earth he was denying. Jin Zixuan took two aggressive strides forward as if to chase them down, then slammed on the brakes, panting heavily from several paces away, the veins bulging across his temple.

After an agonizing silence, he roared at the canopy:

"That's not it, Lady Jiang! It wasn't my mother! It wasn't her idea! It's not forced—I'm not being forced at all!!"

He caught his breath, his face contorting as he screamed:

"It was me! It was my own idea! I wanted you to come on my own!!!"

Jiang Yanli stood entirely frozen. Beside her, Wei Wuxian stared with his jaw slack, while Madame Jin and Jin Zixun looked as though they’d been struck by lightning, neither able to muster a single word.

Having blasted those confessions across the mountain, Jin Zixuan’s fair face detonated into a shade of violent, boiling scarlet, looking as though he might bleed straight from his pores.

He stumbled backward, bracing a hand against an old tree trunk just to keep his knees from buckling. Looking up, he froze. It was as if his brain had finally registered the fact that there were dozens of people staring at him, and that he had just screamed his deepest insecurities to the entire cultivation world. He stood paralyzed in pure shock for three excruciating seconds, let out a strangled, panicked yell, spun on his heel, and bolted through the brush like his robes were on fire.

A thick, stunned hush hung over the trees before Madame Jin’s roar shattered the quiet: "You absolute idiot! What the hell are you running for?!"

She gave Jiang Yanli’s hand a frantic squeeze. "A-Li, we’ll finish talking back at the pavilion! Let me go drag that fool back first!" Without wasting another breath, she summoned her spiritual blade, taking to the air with her retinue in hot pursuit, shouting her son's name as they vanished over the tree line.

Wei Wuxian stood there, blinking blankly at the empty sky, caught between sheer bewilderment and hysterical laughter. "What the hell was that circus? Come on, Shijie, let's go."

Jiang Yanli stood in a daze for a second before giving a quiet, distracted nod.

Wei Wuxian threw a wave over his shoulder at Lan Wangji. "Lan Zhan, I'm heading out!"

Lan Wangji offered a subtle nod, saying nothing, his gaze quietly following their retreating figures until the two vanished beneath the emerald canopy. Over on the other side of the glade, Jin Guangyao had failed to pacify Jin Zixun and his faction; the group flew off on their swords, muttering bitter complaints, leaving the clearing significantly emptier. The remaining spectators, realizing the show was over, began drifting back to the hunt.

Wiping a bead of sweat from his brow, Jin Guangyao offered a wry, exhausted smile. "Well... that was quite something."

Lan Xichen patted his shoulder gently. "What happened today was hardly your fault."

Jin Guangyao sighed, pinching the bridge of his nose. "I'm afraid half an incense stick won't cut it to fix the perimeter."

Lan Xichen asked, "Why is that?"

"It's not just Young Master Wei sweeping up a third of the game," Jin Guangyao explained with a headache. "Da-ge also practically cleared out the vast majority of the feral beasts and monsters on his own."

Lan Xichen couldn't help but chuckle. "That sounds like Da-ge."

Beside them, Lan Wangji’s eyes flickered with quiet contemplation.

Jin Guangyao massaged his temples. "Which means the boundaries of the hunting grounds will need to be pushed out considerably further."

"Then let us see to it at once," Lan Xichen offered.

Jin Guangyao bowed slightly, full of apologies. "Forgive me, Er-ge. You came to participate in the hunt, yet here I am roping you into manual labor."

Lan Xichen smiled warmly. "Think nothing of it. Wangji, should we go on ahead, or will you be joining us?"

Lan Wangji silently drew Bichen, letting the pale blue glare hum in his palm. "I will assist."

Once their swords sliced into the clouds, only a few stray cultivators remained in the glade, trading idle gossip. A moment later, a pair of boots crunched through the underbrush, and Jiang Cheng stepped into the clearing, pausing at the sight of the deserted grounds.

He’d heard whispers on the mountain about a duel between Lan Wangji and Jin Zixuan, and worried that Jiang Yanli was caught in the crossfire, had rushed over to check. He was clearly too late; the crowd had already dispersed. Spotting Sect Leader Yao among the few lingering faces, Jiang Cheng asked, "Sect Leader Yao, what happened here just now?"

Sect Leader Yao cast an oily, loaded look his way. "Ah, Sect Leader Jiang. That Wei Wuxian of your sect... is quite the character, isn't he?"

Jiang Cheng’s brow furrowed. "What do you mean by that?"

Sect Leader Yao gave a hearty, dismissive chuckle. "Oh, far be it from me to speak out of turn. Sect Leader Jiang, pay my idle words no mind!"

Jiang Cheng’s expression iced over. Knowing damn well nothing good was going to come out of the man's mouth, he decided he'd settle the score with Wei Wuxian directly rather than waste his breath playing word games with hypocrites. He wheeled around and marched out of the trees.

Yet as he walked, hushed murmurs drifted on the wind from behind him—huddled low, as if terrified he might hear, yet his sharp spiritual senses picked up every single syllable with razor-sharp clarity.

A clan leader muttered with thick envy, "Lotus Pier really stole the show this time, didn't they? Every fierce corpse and ghost on the mountain marched straight into the Yunmeng Jiang camp of their own accord. Plenty of rogue cultivators will be flocking to join his banner after this."

Sect Leader Yao scoffed, "What can you do? It's not like the rest of us have a Wei Wuxian to lean on."

"Having a Wei Wuxian isn't necessarily a blessing. I certainly wouldn't want a rogue like that stirring up trouble under my roof every single day."

"The arrogance on that boy is insufferable... Fine by me; from now on, if he’s attending a night-hunt, I’m sitting it out."

Another sneered coldly, "Heh. Flocking to the Jiang Clan? Don't flatter them. Strip away the fluff, and they're running straight toward Wei Wuxian. Wasn't it entirely thanks to Wei Wuxian that the Yunmeng Jiang Clan clawed its name back during the Sunshot Campaign anyway...?"

Jiang Cheng walked on, a suffocating, leaden darkness settling over his frame.

It felt as though a dark, unshakeable shadow had fallen across his face—and sunk deep into the hollow of his chest.
